claims.text: Conventionally cast or homogenized Al0.3CoCrFeNi has a coarse-grained initial microstructure.
Room-temperature HPT to an equivalent strain above 100 followed by annealing at approximately 400°C for 30–60 minutes produces an ultrafine or nanocrystalline microstructure in Al0.3CoCrFeNi.
The proposed HPT and annealing treatment produces a high density of coherent twins.
The proposed treatment increases yield strength by approximately 50% relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed treatment maintains or improves tensile ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed treatment produces a consistent or slightly increased Young’s modulus relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed treatment enhances fracture toughness or fracture resistance relative to the untreated alloy.
Grain refinement increases yield strength through the Hall–Petch mechanism.
A high density of grain boundaries and twins enhances strain accommodation.
Grain boundaries and twins enhance energy absorption.
Enhanced strain accommodation and energy absorption at grain and twin boundaries improve ductility and fracture resistance.
Annealing at approximately 400°C for 30–60 minutes relieves excessive internal stresses and thereby recovers ductility.
The proposed low-temperature annealing window preserves the HPT-refined microstructure without significant grain growth.
Higher annealing temperatures or prolonged annealing cause grain coarsening and loss of the ultrafine structure.
Nonuniform HPT processing can prevent uniform microstructural refinement and the expected property improvements.
The coarse-grained untreated alloy has lower yield strength than the proposed treated state.
The coarse-grained untreated alloy has a less favorable combination of ductility and fracture resistance than the proposed treated state.
The processing method may not transfer directly from Al0.3CoCrFeNi to other high-entropy-alloy compositions without adjustment.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis states that Young’s modulus is improved, whereas the predicted outcome allows it merely to remain consistent; unchanged modulus is not an improvement.
The hypothesis states that ductility is improved, while the predicted outcome relaxes this to maintained or improved ductility.
